questions.subject: CYBERSECURITY
questions.topic: An edge configuration with no body limit and no connection cap
questions.learningObjective: Explain why an edge without limits fails in the worst case
questions.stem: Explain why an edge configuration with no body limit and no connection cap fails in the worst case.

answer.exemplar: With neither limit in place, a single client controls both dimensions of the load the edge carries: how many connections exist, and how many bytes each of them holds. Those two quantities multiply, so a modest number of clients can fill the edge's memory and every connection it has, and other clients are refused because nothing is left. A body limit alone still leaves many large bodies possible, and a connection cap alone still leaves a large body possible on each permitted connection, so neither limit on its own would have prevented that outcome.

questions.explanation: Body size and connection count multiply under load, so with neither bounded one source can take the whole edge. A cap alone still permits large bodies, and a size limit alone still permits many bodies.
questions.hint: Ask which two quantities multiply under load.

questions.subject: CYBERSECURITY
questions.topic: A quantifier nested inside another quantifier
questions.learningObjective: Explain why nesting quantifiers multiplies matching work
questions.stem: Explain why a quantifier nested inside another quantifier multiplies the work a matcher does.

answer.exemplar: An outer quantifier repeats a group, and the group it repeats contains a quantifier of its own, so the matcher must decide how many times to repeat the inner part on each of the outer repetitions. Each outer choice is paired with every inner choice, so the total number of possibilities is the product of the two counts rather than their sum. A short record can therefore cost a large number of checks, and the cost grows even though the record never changes size.

questions.explanation: Outer and inner repetition choices pair up, so the possibilities multiply rather than add. That is why a nested quantifier makes short records expensive to validate.
questions.hint: Think about how the two repetition counts combine.

questions.topic: A pool that leaks a slot when the handler returns early
questions.learningObjective: Explain how a slowly leaking pool degrades over a long shift
questions.stem: Explain how a pool that leaks a slot on an early return degrades over a long shift.

answer.exemplar: Each early return leaves one slot checked out forever, so the pool shrinks a little at every occurrence rather than failing loudly. The service keeps serving until the remaining slots are fewer than the concurrent demand, at which point callers block waiting for a slot that will not come back. Because the loss is spread thinly across the shift, the first symptoms look like a gradual traffic increase rather than a leak, and the pool is often blamed for being sized too small.

questions.explanation: A leaked slot is never returned, so capacity shrinks slowly and then falls off a cliff. The gradual shape hides the leak behind an apparent traffic growth problem.
questions.hint: Think about what happens to a slot that is never returned.

questions.subject: CYBERSECURITY
questions.topic: An edge configuration with no body limit and no connection cap
questions.learningObjective: Explain why an unlimited edge collapses under a burst
questions.stem: Explain why an edge with no body limit and no connection cap fails badly under a burst.

answer.exemplar: An edge without a body limit lets a single request occupy as much memory as the client chooses to send, and an edge without a connection cap lets one client open as many connections as it likes. Under a burst those two unbounded quantities multiply, so a modest number of clients can fill the edge's memory and every connection it has, and other clients are refused because nothing is left. Neither limit on its own would have prevented that outcome: the body limit alone still allows many large bodies, and the connection cap alone still allows a large body on each of the permitted connections, so the edge needs both to keep one noisy source from taking it over.

questions.explanation: Body size and connection count are the two factors that multiply, and with neither bounded one source can take the whole edge. Both limits are needed to stop that.
questions.hint: Ask which two quantities multiply under load.
